examples: The fat bear ate berries all autumn.
He carried a fat book of fairy tales.
A fat cloud sat over the hill.

easy.def: Oily stuff in food or in the body.
examples: Butter has fat.
Bears store fat for winter.
Fat keeps seals warm.

more.def: A soft, oily substance found in animals and some plants, which gives the body energy.
examples: Whales have a thick layer of fat that keeps them warm.
Butter and oil are mostly fat.
Bears store fat before the long winter sleep.
The fall was fatal.
The disease was fatal.
The mushroom was fatal.

more.def: Causing someone to die, or having very bad results.
examples: Some wild mushrooms are fatal.
The disease was once fatal.
A fatal mistake cost them the game.

easy.def: What happens to someone in the end.
examples: The sailor's fate was a mystery.
It was their fate to meet again.
No one knew the fate of the lost kitten.

more.def: The things that will happen to someone, which some people believe are decided ahead of time.
examples: The old story tells the fate of a brave knight.
Some people believe fate brought two friends together.
The fate of the old ship was never found.
They were fated to meet.
A fated trip.
It was a fated day.

more.def: Decided in advance by luck or destiny, as if it was meant to happen.
examples: They felt fated to become friends.
The fated meeting changed her life.
In the story, the prince was fated to be king.
It was a fateful day.
A fateful choice.
The fateful meeting.

more.def: Having a big and important result, often a sad one.
examples: It was a fateful day that changed their lives.
A fateful decision led to the shipwreck.
The two friends had a fateful meeting.

easy.def: A man who has a child.
examples: My father is tall.
Her father is a baker.
I help my father cook.

more.def: A man who has a child, or a male parent.
examples: My father reads me a story every night.
The father bird brought a worm to the nest.
She helped her father plant tomatoes in the garden.
He enjoys fatherhood.
Fatherhood is a big job.
Fatherhood is full of love.

more.def: The state of being a father.
examples: He enjoys fatherhood and loves his kids.
Fatherhood changed the way he spent his weekends.
The story shows the joys of fatherhood.
He gave fatherly advice.
A fatherly hug.
His fatherly smile.

more.def: Like a father in being kind and caring.
examples: He gave her fatherly advice.
The fatherly coach hugged the team.
A fatherly smile came from the old man.
I cannot fathom it.
She could not fathom the puzzle.
He fathomed the answer.

more.def: To understand something that is hard, strange or very deep.
examples: I cannot fathom how big the universe really is.
She could not fathom why the door had been left open.
The sailors tried to fathom the depth of the sea.

easy.def: A measure of water depth, six feet.
examples: The water is ten fathoms deep.
A fathom is six feet.
They measured the fathom.

more.def: A unit used to measure the depth of water, equal to six feet.
examples: The sailors measured the water at ten fathoms deep.
A fathom is a measure of six feet used at sea.
The treasure lay at the bottom, forty fathoms down.
The hikers felt fatigue.
Fatigue made him sleepy.
Fatigue came after the long walk.

more.def: A feeling of being extremely tired, usually after working hard or being awake for a long time.
examples: After the long hike, fatigue made our legs feel heavy.
She fell asleep right away from fatigue.
Fatigue can make it hard to pay attention in class.
Farmers fatten the pigs.
The squirrel fattened up.
Bears fatten up before winter.

more.def: To make an animal or person fatter, or to grow fatter.
examples: Bears fatten up on fish before winter sleep.
The farmer fed the pigs to fatten them.
The squirrel fattened up on acorns.

easy.def: The part of a sink that you turn to get water.
examples: Turn on the faucet.
The faucet drips.
Turn off the faucet.

more.def: A device with a handle that you turn to let water flow out of a pipe, as in a sink or a bathtub.
examples: I turned on the faucet and filled the glass with water.
The faucet dripped all night.
Dad fixed the leaky faucet.
It was my fault.
The mess is not his fault.
It is nobody's fault.

more.def: The blame or responsibility for something that went wrong.
examples: It was my fault that the cup broke.
Whose fault was it that we were late?
The accident was nobody's fault.

easy.def: Something that is not good about a person or thing.
examples: His only fault is being late.
She has few faults.
One fault of the toy is its weak wheel.

more.def: A weakness or flaw in a person or thing.
examples: One fault in the design was a loose handle.
Being late is his only fault.
The inspector looked for faults in the bridge.
The lamp is faulty.
A faulty switch.
The brakes were faulty.

more.def: Having a fault, so that it does not work properly.
examples: The lamp has a faulty switch, so it will not turn on.
Faulty wiring can be dangerous.
The faulty toy was sent back to the store.

easy.def: All the animals of a place.
examples: The fauna of the forest.
Fauna and flora.
The fauna is rich.

more.def: All the animals that live in a particular place or time.
examples: The fauna of the rain forest includes monkeys and parrots.
Scientists study the fauna of the desert.
Fauna and flora live together in the wild.

easy.def: A kind thing you do for someone.
examples: Can you do me a favor?
She did me a favor.
He asked for a favor.

more.def: A kind act that you do for someone without being paid.
examples: Could you do me a favor and hold the door?
My neighbor did us a favor and fed the cat.
He asked her a favor.
Blue is my favorite color.
This is my favorite bear.
What is your favorite food?

more.def: Liked more than all the others.
examples: My favorite part of the book is the surprise ending.
Her favorite subject in school is science.
We went to our favorite park for the picnic.
A fawn stood in the grass.
The fawn has spots.
We saw a fawn.

more.def: A young deer, usually with white spots on its back.
examples: A spotted fawn hid in the tall grass.
The fawn stayed close to its mother.
A fawn can walk soon after it is born.

easy.def: A paper copy that is sent through a phone line.
examples: I sent a fax.
The fax came to the office.
The fax is on the desk.

more.def: A copy of a page that is sent over a telephone line by a machine.
examples: The office sent a fax to the bank.
The fax came in this morning.
Dad sent a fax of the form.
